# Remote-procedure call (RPC)

Last updated ||View as Markdown|Agent setup

Workers provide a built-in, JavaScript-native RPC (Remote Procedure Call) ↗ system, allowing you to:

 Define public methods on your Worker that can be called by other Workers on the same Cloudflare account, via Service Bindings
 Define public methods on Durable Objects that can be called by other workers on the same Cloudflare account that declare a binding to it.

results.content:
In practice, the quality of your RPC layer can make or break a project: low latency, stable uptime, and resilient performance under congestion are essential to ensure that users experience Solana as it was designed, fast, seamless, and reliable.

## #What is a Solana RPC?

A Solana Remote Procedure Call (RPC) is the fundamental gateway for any application to interact with the Solana blockchain. It's the protocol powering all dApp-to-chain interactions whether querying balances, submitting transactions, or subscribing to events. RPC nodes do not participate in consensus but specialize in serving API traffic swiftly and reliably.

## Set up your Solana server in minutes [...] ## #Understanding the Role of Solana RPC in DApp Development

Whether you’re building a latency-sensitive trading bot, scaling a wallet to millions of users, or indexing on-chain data for analytics, understanding the RPC landscape will help you make informed choices and architect dApps that can truly scale.

However, getting the most out of Solana’s architecture requires more than just the chain itself. Developers depend on Remote Procedure Call (RPC) providers to connect their applications to the network, submitting transactions, fetching account data, and powering real-time user experiences. [...] ## #Key Features of a High-Performance Solana RPC Service

For developers, the ideal RPC provider combines speed, resilience, and developer tooling. A top-tier service should deliver ultra-low latency and high throughput, processing requests in milliseconds and scaling to handle thousands per second even during congestion events like NFT mints. Equally important are 99.9%+ uptime guarantees, global node distribution to minimize latency, and access to both full and archive nodes for real-time and historical queries.

results.content:
## Why RPC? (And what is RPC anyway?)

Remote Procedure Calls (RPC) are a way of expressing communications between two programs over a network. Without RPC, you might communicate using a protocol like HTTP. With HTTP, though, you must format and parse your communications as an HTTP request and response, perhaps designed in REST style. RPC systems try to make communications look like a regular function call instead, as if you were calling a library rather than a remote service. The RPC system provides a "stub" object on the client side which stands in for the real server-side object. When a method is called on the stub, the RPC system figures out how to serialize and transmit the parameters to the server, invoke the method on the server, and then transmit the return value back. [...] But an RPC promise is more than just a thenable. It is also a proxy. Like an RPC stub, it has a wildcard property. You can use this to express speculative RPC calls on the eventual result, before it has actually resolved. These speculative calls will be sent to the server immediately, so that they can begin executing as soon as the first RPC has finished there, before the result has actually made its way back over the network to the client.

This feature is also known as "Promise Pipelining". Although it isn't explicitly a security feature, it is commonly provided by object-capability RPC systems like Cap'n Proto.

## The future: Custom Bindings Marketplace? [...] In general, Workers RPC is designed to "just work" using idiomatic JavaScript code, so you shouldn't have to spend too much time looking at docs. We'll give you an overview in this blog post. But if you want to understand the full feature set, check out the documentation.
